correction: The first account correctly described PlantUML's heterogeneous quark ownership but treated one Rust projection as the whole DESCRIPTION path. The duplicate-leaf note-owner counterexamples dispatch through Diagram::Component and are rendered by component.rs. The Component-specific account correction was committed before any production change for this mechanism.
dispatch_scope: This mechanism is intentionally limited to DESCRIPTION inputs that Rust's factory selects as Diagram::Component. A 2026-07-31 binary dispatch survey showed that superficially similar note-owner inputs select Diagram::Class or Diagram::Deployment depending on their other commands. Those paths require separate pre-code accounts and implementations; this record makes no completion claim for them.

java_locations.role: Resolves the explicit note code with quarkInContext(false, ...), rejects an existing quark payload, and creates a LeafType.NOTE entity under the current group.
Defines one heterogeneous immediate-child relation from quark children: notes and ordinary leaves are leafs(), groups are separate, and a surviving note makes its owner nonempty.
Emits owner-local direct leaves inside the open cluster and emits only top-parent leaves through the unpackaged stream.
Computes Magma independently from each group's immediate leafs(); a floating note is eligible unless an explicit link touches it, while an attached note is excluded by its hidden note link.

rust_locations.role: ComponentNote retains text, target and source location but drops the explicit note id and immediate package owner, while ComponentPackage inventories only ordinary component/interface ids.

The parser knows the current package and sometimes records a note id transiently in known_note_ids, but neither fact survives in ComponentNote; multiline `note as ID` does not even retain ID in that transient set.
Named-note identity is guessed later from unknown link endpoints, unlinked named notes are omitted from layout, and package clusters admit only ComponentPackage.components.
Magma inventories only components and interfaces; named floating notes are neither owner-local candidates nor rendered at their solved layout unless a later link allowed their id to be inferred.

claimed_invariant: For DESCRIPTION inputs dispatched as ComponentDiagram, an explicitly named floating note is a first-class leaf with durable id, immediate owner and declaration order. It is laid out exactly once, registered in that owner's cluster, qualified by that owner, excluded from the root stream, and considered only in that owner's standalone Magma set. Attached notes retain their owner for cluster membership but remain non-standalone because their hidden link touches both note and target.
causal_divergence: Rust splits Java's quark-backed Entity relation into ComponentPackage.components plus a flat ComponentDiagram.notes vector. ComponentNote loses both id and owner, so component_named_note_ids can recover only a subset through later unknown endpoints. Consequently an unlinked named note receives no LayoutGraph node, cannot make a note-only owner nonempty, cannot be registered with a cluster, cannot receive an owner-qualified name, and never participates in owner-local Magma. These are downstream symptoms of one missing semantic leaf record rather than independent geometry defects.
planned_model_change: Retain explicit note id and qualified immediate owner in ComponentNote at parse time, including multiline declarations. Build the SVEK leaf plan from owner-local components, interfaces and laid-out notes in declaration order, remapping solved slots back to the renderer's typed vectors. Register every owned laid-out note with its exact package cluster. Derive named-note identity directly from the AST, prefix its SVG qualified name with its owner, include only unlinked floating notes in the matching owner Magma, and paint a standalone named note at its solved layout. Do not solve this by moving SVG output after layout or by globally appending notes.
perturbation_axes: note-only owner versus owner with ordinary leaves
root versus one-level and two-level owners
floating named note versus attached note with hidden link
note before versus after ordinary leaves
two versus three owner-local standalone leaves across the Magma gate
explicit link to a named note versus no link
renamed note, owner and leaf labels
acceptance: A valid note-only owner is a cluster and emits its named note once with an owner-qualified name.
Owned floating notes join only their owner's standalone Magma inventory; root and sibling inventories remain unchanged.
Attached owned notes are cluster members but do not enter Magma because their hidden link makes them non-standalone.
Named notes remain addressable by later links without endpoint auto-creation or post-hoc identity inference.
Existing root attached-note, link-note and named-note behavior remains green.
An independent checker attacks ownership depth, attachment, links, order, Magma cardinality, direction and renamed labels at the exact implementation revision.
declared_residue: A duplicate ordinary leaf being listed by more than one ComponentPackage is a separate first-created-quark ownership mechanism with its own pre-code account.
A genuinely empty package being muted to an EMPTY_PACKAGE leaf is a separate render-role mechanism; it is not evidence that a note-only package is empty.
forbidden_approaches: inferring the note owner from coordinates or the nearest cluster
filtering owned notes out of root painting without registering them in their owner cluster
treating every owned note as standalone and ignoring attached-note links
SVG string reparenting or coordinate translations after layout
fixture aliases, source filenames, expected coordinates, comparator changes or baseline changes
